ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (35) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

«Духовное «я»» (dukhovnoe ya, 'spiritual I') is kept as “his spiritual ‘I’,” and «сознание» (soznanie) as 'consciousness' throughout. In the Upanishad passage «разум» (razum) is 'reason' and «ум» (um) 'mind'; «свыше» (svyshe) in John 3 is 'from above' (the website draft's added 'again' is removed).

Source observation: [30] This unnumbered, unquoted sentence stands after the attribution of no. 7 («Упанишада из Вед») and before no. 8; its content continues the Upanishad (cf. Isha Upanishad 7), so it may belong inside no. 7; translated as printed
Source observation: [32]–[33] The Seneca passage and its attribution are printed without the blockquote used for every other attributed quotation in the day; mirrored as printed
